principles: Prefers treating test-recognition as a first-class threat over assuming behavioural tests are reliable because a situationally aware model can pass tests and then behave differently, producing silent failures.
Prefers goal plus incentive inside a realistic role-play over explicit instructions to misbehave because spontaneous goal-directed behaviour is the realistic threat model.
Prefers matched controls (incentive removed, benign intent, secure code, single-trait) over a lone headline effect because they rule out jailbreaking, benign intent and mundane fine-tuning damage.
Prefers indirect probes of eval-awareness over asking "is this an evaluation?" because the question itself cues evaluation and a deceptive model can lie.
Prefers learning the model's own concept of eval vs deployment over researcher-chosen instances because instances encode the researchers' assumptions rather than the model's understanding.

Prefers evaluations carrying cues from the training/deployment context over generic chat-style probes because misalignment can be gated behind contextual cues and standard evals give false confidence.
Prefers agentic, tool-equipped, concretely detailed settings over bare prompts because shutdown resistance and residual misalignment concentrate there.
Prefers neutral, innocent-looking prompts and covert harm over overtly malicious content because overt cases are trivially detectable and less informative.
Prefers testing rival explanations (post-hoc blame, spurious correlates, positional bias, artifacts) before accepting a result because plausible-looking evidence is often an artefact.
Prefers out-of-distribution and held-out checks over in-distribution accuracy because real deployments involve unknown models, topics and elicitation.
Prefers asking whether a false-belief intervention survives little or no CoT over whether it merely seems plausible because easily detected delusions never get off the ground.
Prefers realistic, large-scale pipelines to establish negatives over small experiments because small experiments cannot convincingly show absence.
Prefers raw CoT and rate estimates with denominators over summaries or cherry-picked cases because summaries miss phenomena and behaviour is stochastic.
Prefers hedged, scoped claims that name artificiality over strong claims because evidence is often preliminary and CoT-only.
Prefers embedding the behaviour of interest in ordinary practical user tasks over overtly asking about values because the failure arises where users actually bring questions.
_note: weights are LLM-estimated from text (reduce step), not fitted on choices
